Subject: Recap: Private deployment & compliance — next steps and questionnaire

Hi Jordan — great conversation today. Quick recap from our side and clear next steps so we can qualify the Private/VPC/on-prem options for Pulse Analytics.

Highlights from the call:
- Pulse is evaluating a private deployment option for certain enterprise customers that mandate isolation (some customers may require air-gapped deployments).
- Compliance scope: GDPR applies (EU data subjects), and several customers will require HIPAA protections — you confirmed PHI will be in scope for those customers.
- Pulse is in the middle of a SOC program: Type I completed earlier this year, Type II target later in 2028 (please confirm exact target).

Action items I captured (owner / timeline):
1) Pulse: share the vendor security questionnaire and a redacted network/architecture diagram (Jordan / by EOW 4/14).
2) Redwood: provide an options summary for Private deployments — VPC topology, on‑prem air‑gapped approach, and a hybrid transit option (Neha + Karthik / by 4/13).
3) Legal/compliance sync: include Samantha (legal) to review any HIPAA-specific controls and DPA language (Jordan to loop in Samantha).
4) Schedule a technical topology workshop to walk through network flows, egress rules, and key management (propose week of 4/18).

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-options.pdf (high-level options) — attached for reference.

Questions we still need answered from Pulse to size and qualify:
- Which regions must remain resident (EU-only, multi-region)?
- Do you require outbound network connectivity? If so, are egress proxies/NAT allowed or must all updates be offline-signed packages (air-gap)?
- Expected throughput (RPS) and typical model sizes so we can recommend GPU footprint and packaging cadence.

I’ve cc’d Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (AE) — we’ll turn around the options doc and checklist, and then propose times for the workshop.

Thanks — Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Neha — thanks for the clear recap and for the deck. A few items from our side:

SOC / Compliance:
- We completed SOC 2 Type I in Feb 2028; Type II is targeted for Dec 2028 (internal target). Happy to provide the SOC narrative and the auditor contact once Type II testing begins.
- GDPR: yes — we process EU personal data for EU customers. We have a DPA template and data flow diagrams we can share.
- HIPAA: confirmed. For customers where PHI is involved we must meet HIPAA safeguards; we’ll need encryption at rest/in motion, KMS control, and detailed access audit logs.

Air-gap / Deployment Requirements:
- A subset of our customers (medical devices partners) require an air-gapped on‑prem option for model inference.
- For other enterprise customers, a VPC private deployment with no public subnets and egress via a customer VPN or proxy is acceptable.

Attachments: I’m attaching our vendor security questionnaire (Pulse-vendor-questionnaire.pdf) and a redacted current architecture diagram (pulse-current-arch-v1.png).

Next steps from Pulse: I’ll ask Samantha to review the DPA and add legal comments. We’ll upload the questionnaire and diagram to the shared Drive folder by EOD 4/14.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment & compliance — next steps and questionnaire

Jordan / Neha — looping in some technical notes and initial asks from engineering so we can size and propose a concrete topology in the workshop. High level options we’d recommend to start with: 

Option A — VPC private deployment (recommended for most customers)
- Redwood-managed control plane (optionally private) + customer VPC where inference pods run in private subnets.
- Egress patterns: (1) customer-managed NAT/egress proxy (preferred) OR (2) controlled egress to a dedicated Redwood egress endpoint over a TLS-only channel.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS preferred for PHI; we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) integrations.
- Audit: we expose token-level audit logs and per-request tracing.

Option B — On‑prem air‑gapped appliance
- Offline update model: signed artifact bundles shipped or pulled via a controlled mediate host.
- No outbound internet from inference hosts; updates and telemetry are batched and exported via customer-controlled media.
- Requires an on‑prem ops runbook and occasional physical or logical access for updates.

Option C — Hybrid (dedicated transit / peered egress)
- For customers that want central control but restrict some tenants to air-gapped infra; we can route selective workloads to on-prem while keeping control plane in a private region.

Technical asks for the workshop / to prepare a proposal:
- Redacted network diagram with: subnets, egress points, existing VPN/Direct Connect, and any OCI/GCP/Azure peering details.
- Typical request patterns (RPS, percent of requests requiring PHI processing), average and 99th perc token lengths, and model family(s) you expect to run.
- List of required logs/audit retention windows and any SIEM/collector endpoints (e.g., Splunk, Sumo).
- Clarify whether the customer expects complete zero‑trust segmentation between inference and other app tiers.

I attached a short checklist (private-deploy-checklist.xlsx) that maps these asks to owners and helps speed the readiness review. If Pulse can fill the checklist ahead of the workshop it will make the session much more productive.

Happy to present the three options and the tradeoffs (latency / cost / operational burden) during the workshop. Proposed duration: 60–90 minutes with engineering + security + network representation from Pulse.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
